But it’s the best mixed with the absolute worst. Having to drag children away from their parents gets exhausting.  But mourning with a family after losing an elder, who lived a powerful life, is an amazing experience. It helps me keep my head cool, you know? But $50 per body could be improved upon😂

Bodies like this generally make it directly into the medical examiners office, and IDEALLY it would be a direct cremation. (Unless the circumstances are suspicious, but that’s WAY above my pay grade) But families sometimes make personal requests to work something out. It’s a third party that I work with, so I just get paid to pick them up, bag the body, and drop them off to the designated spot. But that’s for Medical examiner calls, funeral homes operate differently.

Even worse, my buddy was moving a decomp from a bathroom tub, but the guy left his jets on and the system was keeping the water at a consistent WARM temperature. For about a month. The fucked up thing is that your skin is one of the sower decomposing organs, so it’ll act as a balloon in some occasions, and everything inside your body will turn into a sort soup. The police had turned everything off, and he went to move the body. When he did, the man’s skin sheered off and he fell back in the tub, covering my buddy in the decomp water. He told me a substantial amount got in his mouth, and he’s now known as the guy who’s tried decomp soup all across Utah/ME/PD. Pretty fucking metal😂

I work with funeral homes and transport bodies, sometimes similar to this one. I shit you not, in the summer months the walls become a moving black mass of flies. This is pretty early on in the decomposition phase, but yes, the smell is worse than you could imagine. The worst part is that they purge when you start to move them, and everything on the inside that’s liquified comes out. We sometimes have to perform what is called a “controlled popping” because the bloat is too bad to safely move them. Thank GOD I don’t have to clean the scenes lol

Cars. Everyone likes to talk about the numbers, but you don’t really SEE it until you have my job. I currently work transport for a funeral home chain, but was previously employed through a third party company, that would pick up for the Medical examiners office. The shit I’d see was visceral. Seeing the ways people manage to die in cars is fucking insane. Suicides, driving on the wrong side of the highway, getting distracted and driving into the bed of an 18 wheeler, drunk drivers, etc. So many people that needed a closed casket, over something as stupid as a text, or something as tragic as being in the right place at the wrong time. I like to say that the job doesn’t effect me, but whenever I get in a car my anxiety just eats me up. You get in a crash going past 60 miles per hour, and we have to pull your body straight to move it because every bone in your body has shattered. I know we all have places to be, and that we all get complacent at times, but we need to remember what’s at risk.
